lessons.name: LeRobot community (Hugging Face)
lessons.summary: The LeRobot community is the open group of developers, students, and labs who build, test, and share data for Hugging Face's LeRobot library.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

The LeRobot community is the open group of developers, students, and labs who build, test, and share data for Hugging Face's LeRobot library.

![Participants of the LeRobot hackathon hub at 42 Paris, June 2025](/img/lessons/orgs_other-lerobot-community.webp)
*Participants of the LeRobot hackathon hub at 42 Paris, June 2025. Source: [42AI LeRobot Hackathon post](https://42-ai.github.io/posts/LeRobotHackathon/), CC BY 4.0, Mathieu Perez.*

## What they do in robotics

- **One shared workflow:** the docs describe Teleoperate → Record → Train → Deploy for real robots such as the **SO-101** arm.
- **Open code:** `huggingface/lerobot` is Apache-2.0 and welcomes fixes, docs, datasets, and support for new hardware.
- **Shared datasets:** members publish robot demonstrations on the Hugging Face Hub, much like publishing packages to npm.
- **Worldwide hackathons:** on June 14–15, 2025, teams worked online and in local hubs and submitted a dataset plus a short video.

> **Key idea:** LeRobot grows through its users: every published dataset or fix makes the next robot experiment cheaper.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **42 Paris already hosted a hub:** 42AI's highlights post lists four 42 Paris teams in the top 30, with LeChef first and LeSplat third.
- **Same hardware as the lab:** the project "Assemble & teleoperate an SO-101" starts on this stack.
- **Visibility:** public datasets and demo videos show the lab's work to a global audience.

## How to engage

1. **Join the LeRobot Discord** linked from the docs; hackathon voting and help happen there.
2. **Reproduce one tutorial end to end** before changing any code.
3. **Publish a small, well-described dataset** on the Hub.
4. **Open a focused pull request**, such as a doc fix or a clear bug reproduction.

lessons.name: Open Source Robotics Foundation (Open Robotics)
lessons.summary: Open Robotics, the Open Source Robotics Foundation, is the nonprofit that stewards ROS, Gazebo, and related open-source robot software.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Open Robotics, the Open Source Robotics Foundation, is the nonprofit that stewards ROS, Gazebo, and related open-source robot software.

![A simple mobile manipulator robot with gripper, sensor, and wheels in the Gazebo simulator](/img/lessons/orgs_other-open-robotics.webp)
*A simple mobile manipulator robot with gripper, sensor, and wheels in the Gazebo simulator. Source: [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Gazebo_7_Simple_mobile_manipulator.png), Apache License 2.0, Jose Luis Rivero.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Stewards core tools:** ROS (a software development kit for robot apps), Gazebo (a simulator), ros-controls (real-time control), and Open-RMF (coordinating robot fleets).
- **Runs shared infrastructure:** build servers and continuous integration for these projects.
- **Shares governance:** the **Open Source Robotics Alliance (OSRA)**, launched in 2024, gives companies and contributors a formal voice.
- **Runs ROSCon:** the next global edition is planned for Kraków, October 12–14, 2027.

Think of it like a language foundation: it maintains the interpreter and the package index so everyone else can build on them.

> **Key idea:** Most robot software you will touch, from ROS 2 nodes to Gazebo worlds, traces back to projects Open Robotics stewards.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Shared vocabulary:** nodes, topics, and simulated worlds appear in many lab projects and partner codebases.
- **Simulation first:** Gazebo lets teams break code safely before touching real hardware.

> **Watch out:** Open Robotics is not Intrinsic. Intrinsic acquired the commercial subsidiary in December 2022; the foundation continued separately.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the project-update keynote** to see what ROS 2 and Gazebo ship next.
2. **Attend a ROSCon** or a regional edition, such as ROSCon JP.
3. **Read the OSRA pages** to see how technical committees and contributors steer projects.

lessons.name: OROCA
lessons.summary: OROCA is a Korean volunteer community for open-source robotics software and hardware, built around a large online forum and GitHub projects.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

OROCA is a Korean volunteer community for open-source robotics software and hardware, built around a large online forum and GitHub projects.

![Building an iTurtle robot at the Seoul Hardware Hackathon](/img/lessons/orgs_other-oroca.webp)
*Building an iTurtle robot at the Seoul Hardware Hackathon. Source: [oroca/iTurtle on GitHub](https://github.com/oroca/iTurtle), Apache License 2.0 (repository license), OROCA iTurtle contributors.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Runs a large forum:** the Naver cafe 오로카 opened on December 25, 2012 and showed 49,558 members, with boards on ROS, microcontrollers, and local groups.
- **Publishes open projects:** ROS tutorials, `oroca-ros-pkg`, OROCA-EduBot, and **iTurtle**, a miniature **TurtleBot3**-based robot from the Pangyo local group.
- **Hosts seminars:** its YouTube channel shares Open Robotics Seminar talks, such as game engines for ROS 2 simulation.

It works like a regional Stack Overflow plus meetup: people ask, answer, and then build together offline.

> **Key idea:** A forum, local groups, and small open robots can turn beginners into contributors.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **A community model:** 42AI could copy the mix of forum, local groups, and seminars in Paris.
- **Low-cost designs:** iTurtle shows how a small TurtleBot3-style robot can serve as a shared learning platform.

> **Watch out:** Most material is in Korean, some repositories are old, and the oroca.org domain now hosts unrelated content. Current project activity is unknown.

## How to engage

1. **Browse the GitHub organization** for tutorials and robot designs.
2. **Read public forum boards** with a translator.
3. **Open an issue or pull request** on iTurtle; its README invites both.

lessons.name: Poppy Project
lessons.summary: Poppy Project is an open-source, 3D-printed robot platform, born in 2012 at Inria's Flowers lab, for research, education, and art.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Poppy Project is an open-source, 3D-printed robot platform, born in 2012 at Inria's Flowers lab, for research, education, and art.

![An open-source, 3D-printed Poppy humanoid robot](/img/lessons/orgs_other-poppy-project.webp)
*An open-source, 3D-printed Poppy humanoid robot. Source: [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Open-Source_3D_printed_Poppy_humanoid_robot.jpg), CC BY-SA 4.0, Inria / Poppy-project.org / Photo H. Raguet.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Open robot designs:** **Poppy Humanoid** and **Poppy Ergo Jr** repositories share printable parts, assembly notes, and software.
- **Poppy Ergo Jr:** a small 6-joint arm using low-cost Dynamixel XL-320 motors, a Raspberry Pi, and swappable lampshade, grasper, or pen-holder tools.
- **The pypot library:** a Python library for controlling Dynamixel motors.

Like an open-source app with its build files included: you print the parts, flash the software, and own the whole stack.

> **Key idea:** Poppy proved that a research-grade humanoid can be fully open: printable, documented, and forkable.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **A French open-hardware reference:** a nearby example of publishing robots, not just code.
- **Design lessons:** the README states a full humanoid cost $8000–9000, about 60% for 25 Dynamixel actuators, so actuators dominate budgets.

> **Watch out:** poppy-project.org no longer resolves and Ergo Jr was last updated in May 2022. Treat Poppy as a historical design; current maintenance is unknown.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the Humanoid overview** to see the robot move.
2. **Read the Ergo Jr repository** for a cheap arm design.
3. **Try pypot** with any Dynamixel motor you have.

lessons.name: PX4 open-source community
lessons.summary: The PX4 community is a global group of developers and companies building open-source flight-control software for drones and other unmanned vehicles.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

The PX4 community is a global group of developers and companies building open-source flight-control software for drones and other unmanned vehicles.

![A Pixhawk flight controller board, the open hardware PX4 often runs on](/img/lessons/orgs_other-px4.webp)
*A Pixhawk flight controller board, the open hardware PX4 often runs on. Source: [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Pixhawk.png), CC BY 4.0, Pixhawk project authors.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Builds an autopilot:** PX4 runs drones, rovers, boats, and underwater vehicles, from consumer to industrial uses.
- **Neutral home:** the project is hosted by the **Dronecode Foundation** under the Linux Foundation, not owned by one company.
- **Big, active codebase:** Dronecode's 2025 review counts 651 contributors from 99 organizations and PX4 v1.16 with new rover support and better **ROS 2** integration.

An autopilot is like an operating system for a vehicle: it reads sensors, estimates position, and drives motors many times per second.

> **Key idea:** PX4 lets a small team fly real vehicles without writing flight control from scratch.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Simulation first:** PX4 docs support simulators such as Gazebo, so teams can fly in software before buying a drone.
- **Ties to ROS 2:** drone projects can share tooling with arm and rover projects.

## How to engage

1. **Set up the development environment** with the official Getting Started guide.
2. **Fly in simulation** before touching hardware.
3. **Join Discord** and the weekly developer call, which is open to all.
4. **Report bugs on GitHub** with logs and steps to reproduce.

lessons.name: ROS Japan Users Group
lessons.summary: The ROS Japan Users Group (ROS Japan UG) is a volunteer community that runs ROS study sessions, talk nights, and hackathons in Japan.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

The ROS Japan Users Group (ROS Japan UG) is a volunteer community that runs ROS study sessions, talk nights, and hackathons in Japan.

![Logo of the ROS Japan Users Group](/img/lessons/orgs_other-ros-japan-ug.webp)
*Logo of the ROS Japan Users Group. Source: [rosjp on GitHub](https://github.com/rosjp), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Regular meetups:** its Connpass page lists numbered events, such as #63, a ROS lightning-talk night, and #64, a themed special in Shibuya, Tokyo.
- **Hackathons:** #62 was a hackathon restricted to vibe coding.
- **Open channels:** talks on YouTube, code on GitHub, and chat moving from Slack to a Japan channel on Open Robotics' Zulip.

It is a user group, like a local Python meetup: it does not build ROS itself, but helps people learn and use it.

> **Key idea:** User groups turn a huge framework like ROS into small, friendly sessions where beginners can ask questions.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **A template for the lab:** numbered events, lightning talks, and themed hackathons are easy to copy in Paris.
- **Network:** ROSCon JP 2027 runs in Osaka on May 20–21, 2027, co-hosted with Open Robotics.

## How to engage

1. **Watch a recorded LT night** to see the talk format.
2. **Join the Japan channel on Zulip** to follow events.
3. **Register on Connpass** to get notified about upcoming events.

lessons.name: ROS-Industrial Consortium Europe
lessons.summary: ROS-Industrial Consortium Europe (RIC-EU) is the European branch of ROS-Industrial, led by Fraunhofer IPA in Stuttgart, helping factories adopt ROS 2.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

ROS-Industrial Consortium Europe (RIC-EU) is the European branch of ROS-Industrial, led by Fraunhofer IPA in Stuttgart, helping factories adopt ROS 2.

![A talk at the ROS-Industrial Europe Conference 2025 in Strasbourg](/img/lessons/orgs_other-ric-europe.webp)
*A talk at the ROS-Industrial Europe Conference 2025 in Strasbourg. Source: [ROS-Industrial blog](https://rosindustrial.org/news/2026/2/17/ros-2-in-industry-key-takeaways-from-the-ros-industrial-conference-2025), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Member consortium:** companies and researchers share the cost of tools industry needs; members get support, training, and joint projects.
- **One of three regions:** SwRI leads the Americas consortium and A*STAR's ARTC leads Asia-Pacific.
- **Annual conference:** the 13th edition, in Strasbourg in November 2025, covered drivers, real-time control, and humanoid safety.

It is like an industry working group for an open-source framework: users pool money to fix the gaps that matter to them.

> **Key idea:** RIC-EU is where open-source robot software meets factory requirements like determinism and long-term maintenance.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Industry insight:** talks show what companies expect from ROS 2 in production.
- **European network:** the 2026 conference runs at Fraunhofer IPA on December 3–4, with lab tours.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the EU consortium update** on the ROS-I channel.
2. **Read the conference recap** for current industrial topics.
3. **Join the monthly developers meeting**, listed on the events page.

lessons.name: Webots open-source community
lessons.summary: The Webots open-source community is the group of users and contributors around Webots, a free robot simulator released as open source in December 2018.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

The Webots open-source community is the group of users and contributors around Webots, a free robot simulator released as open source in December 2018.

![The Webots interface with a simulated car, scene tree, and code editor](/img/lessons/orgs_other-webots.webp)
*The Webots interface with a simulated car, scene tree, and code editor. Source: [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Wbinterface.png), CC BY-SA 4.0, DavidMansolino.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Maintains a simulator:** Webots models, programs, and simulates robots, vehicles, and mechanical systems on Windows, Linux, and macOS.
- **Many languages:** controllers can be written in C, C++, Python, Java, MATLAB, or with **ROS**.
- **Works in the open:** the `cyberbotics/webots` repository is Apache-2.0, with issues, Discussions, and a contributing guide.

A simulator is like a test environment for robots: you can crash a virtual robot a thousand times for free.

> **Key idea:** Webots gives beginners a ready-made world with robots, sensors, and physics, so they can write controller code on day one.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Fast onboarding:** the official Tutorial 1 builds a first simulation with an e-puck robot in about 30 minutes.
- **Hardware-free practice:** teams can test ideas before touching a real robot.

> **Watch out:** the community is distinct from Cyberbotics' paid support; for free help, use GitHub Discussions and issues.

## How to engage

1. **Do Tutorial 1** from the official guide.
2. **Ask questions in GitHub Discussions.**
3. **Report reproducible bugs** or improve docs following CONTRIBUTING.md.
